B250: A Better Homes & Gardens collection of bread recipes for home bakers. It covers yeast loaves, quick breads, rolls, and flatbreads, with step by step guidance written for cooks at a range of skill levels.
B238: Molly Baz's 2021 cookbook is built around approachable recipes and a conversational teaching style. Baz, a former Bon Appétit editor, organizes the book around techniques and flavor ideas that help home cooks improvise with confidence in their own kitchens.
B276: Eaten is an independent magazine about the history and culture of food, published in issue form. Number five, from Spring and Summer 2019, collects essays and illustrated features that trace how particular dishes, ingredients, and eating habits developed over time.
B292: Gordon Ramsay: Kitchen Heaven is a cookbook by the Scottish chef, with recipes drawn from his restaurant career and his home cooking. It covers starters, mains, and desserts, and pairs each recipe with Ramsay's tips on technique and ingredients.
B245: Home Made is a cookbook by Dutch food writer and illustrator Yvette van Boven. Her recipes are arranged around everyday cooking at home, and the book mixes her own drawings and photographs with dishes for baking, preserving, and family meals.
B015: The book is a cookbook devoted to lemons, from Gennaro Contaldo, the Italian chef from the Amalfi Coast who mentored Jamie Oliver. Published in English as Gennaro's Limoni, it gathers recipes for small plates, pasta, desserts, drinks, and preserves.
B241: Simple is a cookbook by Yotam Ottolenghi, the London chef and food writer. Each recipe is organized by an acronym of qualities such as short on time, ten ingredients or fewer, or make ahead, so cooks can choose dishes by effort.
B227: Peter Reinhart's The Bread Baker's Apprentice is a guide to making artisan bread at home. It follows the stages of bread making, from mixing and fermentation to shaping and baking, and presents formulas for loaves such as ciabatta, pain au levain, and bagels.
B107: The New Sotheby's Wine Encyclopedia is a reference work by wine writer Tom Stevenson. It surveys the world's wine regions, grape varieties, producers, and winemaking methods, with maps and photographs, and has been revised through several editions.
B258: 419 is a 2012 novel by Canadian author Will Ferguson. It follows a Canadian woman who investigates her father's death after he falls victim to an advance fee email scam, and the story moves between Ontario and Nigeria.
B327: A Song of Stone is a 1997 novel by Iain Banks, published without the M in his byline. Set in a nameless European country torn by civil war, it follows an aristocratic couple in their castle as soldiers take control of their lives.
B281: Brick Lane is the 2003 debut novel by Monica Ali. It follows Nazneen, a Bangladeshi woman who moves to London for an arranged marriage and builds a life in the East End community around Brick Lane.
B306: Dead Souls is an 1842 Russian novel by Nikolai Gogol. Its protagonist, Chichikov, travels the provinces buying the names of dead serfs who still count on tax rolls, and meets a gallery of landowners along the way.
B229: First Person Singular is a 2020 collection of eight short stories by Haruki Murakami. Narrators look back on episodes from their lives, and the settings range from Tokyo to the baseball field to a talking monkey's confession.
B083: Herr Lehmann is a 2001 novel by Sven Regener, the singer of the band Element of Crime. Written in German, it follows Frank Lehmann, a bartender in West Berlin's Kreuzberg district, through the months before the Berlin Wall falls in 1989.
B024: Jesus' Son is a 1992 collection of linked short stories by Denis Johnson. A drifting narrator named Fuckhead recounts episodes of addiction, petty crime, and chance encounters in the American Midwest and Southwest.
B158: Kicking the Sky is a 2013 novel by Canadian author Anthony De Sa. Set in Toronto's Portuguese community in 1977, it follows a boy named Antonio whose neighborhood is shaken by the murder of a young shoeshine worker.
B130: Selected Poems collects work by the American poet E. E. Cummings. It includes his experimental typography, unusual punctuation, and lowercase style, along with love poems, satirical verse, and portraits of city life.
B091: Sämtliche Werke is a German-language edition of the collected works of Nikolai Gogol. The Russian writer's satirical novel Dead Souls, his St. Petersburg tales, and his plays such as The Government Inspector are the central texts in a collection of this kind.
B146: The Crow Road is a 1992 novel by Iain Banks. Prentice McHoan returns to his family's Scottish home and tries to learn what happened to his uncle Rory, who vanished years earlier, while the McHoan and Urvill families go through births, deaths, and weddings.
B134: The Lovely Bones is a 2002 novel by Alice Sebold. Susie Salmon, a girl murdered at age fourteen, narrates from her own heaven as she watches her family and her killer in a Pennsylvania suburb in the 1970s.
B093: The Pickwick Papers is Charles Dickens's first novel, published in serial form in 1836 and 1837. Samuel Pickwick and the members of his club travel through the English countryside and meet a run of comic characters, including the servant Sam Weller.
B061: The Short Stories of Ernest Hemingway collects the American author's short fiction. It includes the Nick Adams stories, tales of war, hunting, and bullfighting, and well known pieces such as The Snows of Kilimanjaro and Hills Like White Elephants.
B182: Through Black Spruce is a 2008 novel by Canadian author Joseph Boyden. Will Bird, a Cree trapper in northern Ontario, lies in a coma while his niece Annie travels to Toronto, Montreal, and New York to search for her missing sister Suzanne.
B233: Berlin Game is the 1983 novel that begins Len Deighton's Bernard Samson series. London intelligence officer Samson goes to East Berlin to extract a valuable agent, and the mission opens a hunt for a mole inside his own department.
B264: Clown Town is a Slough House novel by Mick Herron. The series follows a group of exiled British intelligence officers who have been reassigned to a decaying London office, under their irascible boss Jackson Lamb.
B043: Death and the Oxford Box is a mystery by Veronica Stallwood in her series about the crime novelist Kate Ivory. Set in Oxford, it follows Kate as she gets drawn into an investigation of a death with links to the city's academic world.
B201: Final Orbit is the third Cold War space thriller by Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield, after The Apollo Murders and The Defector. Set around the 1975 Apollo-Soyuz mission, it brings back NASA flight controller Kaz Zemeckis as a deadly accident threatens US and Soviet cooperation.
B230: House of Correction is a 2021 standalone thriller by Nicci French, the pen name of the couple Nicci Gerrard and Sean French. Tabitha Hardy, a woman charged with murder and held in prison, works to prove she has been framed.
B142: Lucky You is a 2000 novel by Carl Hiaasen. Two Florida residents share a winning lottery ticket worth millions, and a pair of white supremacists plan to take the money, which leads to a chase across the state's backroads.
B311: Quite Ugly One Morning is the 1996 debut novel by Scottish author Christopher Brookmyre and the first to feature journalist Jack Parlabane. Parlabane investigates a murder in Edinburgh that leads him toward a conspiracy inside the National Health Service.
B252: Road Dogs is a 2009 novel by Elmore Leonard. Bank robber Jack Foley, newly out of prison, and his former cellmate Cundo Rey, a Cuban con man, settle in Los Angeles, where Foley meets a woman who works as a psychic.
B169: Strandkorbkrimis is a German-language collection of short crime stories set at the Baltic and North Sea coast, where the beach chair, or Strandkorb, is a familiar seaside sight. Several regional anthologies carry this title, and the book appears to be one of that series.
B237: The Department of Rare Books and Special Collections is a 2022 novel by Canadian author Eva Jurczyk. Set at a university library, it follows a librarian who investigates after a valuable manuscript goes missing during a change in the department's leadership.
B067: The Full Cupboard of Life is the fifth novel in Alexander McCall Smith's No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency series. Precious Ramotswe, Botswana's first female private detective, takes on a client who needs to choose among four suitors.
B010: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is the first novel in Stieg Larsson's Millennium series, published in Swedish in 2005. Journalist Mikael Blomkvist and hacker Lisbeth Salander work together to find out what happened to a member of a wealthy industrial family who disappeared decades earlier.
B056: The Sacred Art of Stealing is a 2002 novel by Christopher Brookmyre. Angelique de Xavia, a bank robber who leaves no trace, plans her heists in Glasgow while detective Zoe Cameron and a former thief trail her.
B235: Tokyo Express is a 1958 mystery by Japanese author Seichō Matsumoto. Two detectives take apart an apparent double suicide, and the case turns on a precisely timed railway journey and a seemingly perfect alibi.
B277: Douglas Adams's Starship Titanic is a 1997 novel by Terry Jones, adapted from the computer game that Douglas Adams created. A luxury spaceship leaves for its maiden voyage and malfunctions, and the humans who board it meet a crew of eccentric robots.
B150: Pattern Recognition is a 2003 novel by William Gibson. Cayce Pollard, a marketing consultant with a sensitivity to corporate logos, travels from New York to London, Tokyo, and Moscow to find the maker of a series of mysterious online film fragments.
B032: The Algebraist is a 2004 standalone science fiction novel by Iain M. Banks. Fassin Taak, a scholar, studies the Dwellers who inhabit gas giants, and his research draws him into a war between rival powers over a buried secret.
B033: Virtual Light is a 1993 novel by William Gibson and the first book of his Bridge trilogy. In a near future California, a bicycle courier named Chevette Washington steals a pair of sunglasses that hold valuable data, and she is soon pursued.
B030: Good Omens is a 1990 comic novel written by Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman. An angel and a demon who have grown comfortable on Earth try to head off the end of the world after the Antichrist is misplaced as a baby.
B301: Necrophenia is a 2008 comic fantasy novel by Robert Rankin, set in the author's absurd, pub centered version of Brentford and London. It mixes rock and roll, the walking dead, and time travel in a plot that runs through its protagonist's investigation.
B218: The City of Brass is the 2017 debut novel by S. A. Chakraborty and the first in the Daevabad trilogy. Nahri, a con artist in eighteenth century Cairo, learns she has magical powers and is taken to the hidden djinn city of Daevabad.
B058: The Truth is the twenty-fifth Discworld novel by Terry Pratchett, published in 2000. William de Worde starts the Discworld's first newspaper in Ankh-Morpork, and his reporting draws him into a plot against the city's ruler, Lord Vetinari.
B115: All the Light We Cannot See is a 2014 novel by Anthony Doerr. It alternates between Marie-Laure, a blind French girl, and Werner, a German orphan with a talent for radios, whose paths approach each other in occupied Saint-Malo during World War Two.
B136: Canoe Lake is a 2002 novel by Roy MacGregor, a Canadian journalist and author. It takes the 1917 death of painter Tom Thomson on Ontario's Canoe Lake as its starting point and sets the story in Algonquin Park.
B077: Dodger is a 2012 novel by Terry Pratchett, set in Victorian London. Dodger, a young tosher who scavenges in the sewers, rescues a girl from attackers and meets Charles Dickens and Henry Mayhew among the city's characters.
B280: Heartstone is the fifth novel in C. J. Sansom's Shardlake series, set in 1545. Matthew Shardlake, a hunchbacked lawyer in the court of Henry VIII, travels to Portsmouth while France threatens invasion, and takes on a wardship case there.
B220: Persona Non Grata is the third novel in Ruth Downie's series about Gaius Petreius Ruso, a Roman army doctor. Ruso and his British partner Tilla travel to Gaul, where his family's debts and the death of a creditor force him to investigate.
B299: When Christ and His Saints Slept is a 1993 historical novel by Sharon Kay Penman and the first of her Plantagenet trilogy. It covers the twelfth century civil war in England between Empress Maude and her cousin King Stephen, a period known as the Anarchy.
B198: How to Be a Canadian is a 2001 humor book by brothers Will Ferguson and Ian Ferguson. It describes Canadian habits, history, and regional quirks in a series of comic essays for readers inside and outside the country.
B079: Wortkirmes is a German-language book of humorous verse and wordplay by Robert Gernhardt, a poet, cartoonist, and satirist. It collects poems and short comic pieces that play on language, rhyme, and everyday absurdity.
B120: The Graveyard Book is a 2008 children's novel by Neil Gaiman. A toddler escapes the murder of his family and is raised by the ghosts of a graveyard, where he learns their skills while a killer is still looking for him.
B185: The Sea of Monsters is the second novel in Rick Riordan's Percy Jackson and the Olympians series, published in 2006. Percy and his friends sail into the Sea of Monsters to find the Golden Fleece and save Camp Half-Blood.
B059: In Cold Blood is Truman Capote's 1966 account of the 1959 murder of the Clutter family in Holcomb, Kansas. Capote follows the investigation and the two killers, Perry Smith and Dick Hickock, through their capture, trial, and execution, using the techniques of a novel.
B253: Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil is a 1994 nonfiction book by John Berendt. It records the author's years in Savannah, Georgia, and the murder trials of the antiques dealer Jim Williams, alongside the city's colorful residents.
B262: The Just is a work of narrative nonfiction by Dutch writer Jan Brokken. It tells the stories of diplomats and others who helped Jewish refugees escape Europe during World War Two, including Jan Zwartendijk in Lithuania and Chiune Sugihara.
B174: A Serious Ocean is a sailing book by John Kretschmer, a professional offshore skipper. It covers lessons from his ocean crossings and storms at sea, and from the boats and crews he has sailed with.
B085: Atlas Obscura is a guidebook compiled by Joshua Foer, Dylan Thuras, and Ella Morton, drawn from the Atlas Obscura website. It catalogs hundreds of unusual, hidden, and little known places around the world, with photographs and short descriptions organized by region.
B199: The Complete Notes is an omnibus of travel writing by Bill Bryson. It brings together his humorous accounts of traveling in Britain and the United States, including Notes from a Small Island and Notes from a Big Country.
B178: Dispatches from the Front is the memoir of David Halton, a Canadian broadcast journalist who worked for CBC News. It recounts his reporting from conflicts and political events around the world over a career of several decades.
B112: Life on Air is the 2002 memoir of David Attenborough, the British broadcaster and naturalist. It traces his career at the BBC, from early television work to series such as Life on Earth, and the expeditions he made to film wildlife.
B122: We Were an Island is a biography by Peter P. Blanchard III of Art and Nan Kellam. The couple lived for decades on Placentia Island off the coast of Maine, without electricity, and later gave the island to The Nature Conservancy.
B260: Entangled Life is a 2020 book by biologist Merlin Sheldrake about fungi. It explains how mycelial networks work, how fungi shape ecosystems, and how they bear on medicine, food, and the study of intelligence.
B171: Freakonomics is a 2005 book by economist Steven D. Levitt and journalist Stephen J. Dubner. It applies economic methods to unusual questions, such as the effects of incentives on cheaters, parents, and drug dealers.
B282: The Collection is a book by Peter Ackroyd, the English biographer and novelist. It gathers his journalism, essays, and short fiction, with a range of subjects that includes London, literature, and history.
B211: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance is a 1974 book by Robert M. Pirsig. A father and his son travel across the United States by motorcycle, and the narrator uses the trip to explore questions about quality, values, and his own past.
B251: Principles: Life & Work is a 2017 book by Ray Dalio, founder of the investment firm Bridgewater Associates. It sets out the rules Dalio developed for decision making, relationships, and running an organization, and draws on his experience in finance.
B184: The Entrepreneur's Playbook is a business guide by Leonard C. Green. It lays out steps for starting and running a company, covering planning, funding, and growth, and draws on examples from the author's experience.
B202: Century is a large format photography book edited by Bruce Bernard and published by Phaidon in 1999. It presents images from across the twentieth century, arranged chronologically, covering war, politics, art, and daily life.
B284: 642 Things to Write About is a writing prompt book from the San Francisco Writers' Grotto. It contains hundreds of short exercises that cover fiction, memoir, and poetry, and it leaves space for the writer's own responses.
B209: Model Shop appears to be a book with this title, but the author and edition could not be confirmed. Several works use the name, including the 1969 Jacques Demy film, so the subject remains unclear.
